newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent eases but holds Nov paper premium.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent eases but holds Nov paper premium.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Dated Brent softened in active trade on Monday but held onto a premium to prompt November paper as early month supply remained tight, traders said.

Four cargoes loading November 2-7 were sold to a major for premiums of between 11 and five cents over November. A fifth, due to load November 9-11, went to a Wall Street trader for a two-cent premium.
Wet Brent traded Friday at Nov plus 11 cents.
"Dated came off a bit today but it's still got a healthy premium to the month in question," said a trader.
Only one Brent was due down the paper chains on Tuesday, followed by two on Wednesday, traders said.

Dec Brent gained two cents to $24.55 a barrel by 1730 GMT on Monday. The prompt Nov/Dec intermonth spread slipped below +50 cents after trading at +53 cents while Dec/Jan was pegged at +70 cents, also about three cents down on the day.
Next week's CFDs lost about four cents to talk at Dec Brent +28/+36 cents, but the balance of this week gained about five cents firmer.
Other North Sea grades talked a shade softer but some sellers were reluctant to lower offers.
"I don't see any real reason for the market to come off at the moment but it has gone a long way up so may be due a breather," said a North Sea producer.
Forties was seen losing a couple of cents to Dated Brent +50/+55 cents and Norwegian Statfjord slipping by a similar degree to be valued around Dated Brent +60 cents.
West African crude was firm on shortening supply of November liftings, traders said.
"Off all the main grades, only about half a dozen are left in November," said one.
